{"task": {"id": "I_kwDONElfw88AAAABYb0B6g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlV6PzhB_0aw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlV6P", "number": 88, "title": "Drive MMD kinematic rigid bodies through MotionState instead of per-frame body teleports", "body": "## Problem

The maintainer reports intermittent severe MMD physics breakage, particularly around **120 FPS**. It still happens after [#86 / PR #87](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/pull/87) switched the default runtime to an Ammo-compatible WASM build of newer Bullet, so upgrading Bullet alone did not resolve the observed problem. **The root cause remains unconfirmed.**

A specific implementation difference from **babylon-mmd's native Bullet path** is worth trying as an **actual default change** (not an A/B selector):

- In [three-mmd-loader `RigidBody.updateFromBone()`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts), Type-0 (FollowBone/kinematic) bodies currently update **both** `btRigidBody.setCenterOfMassTransform(...)` and `body.getMotionState().setWorldTransform(...)` on each animation/update frame. This occurs in ordinary `_setTransformFromBone()` and the PMX deferred pre-physics path.
- [babylon-mmd `MmdBulletPhysicsModel.syncBodies()`](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/mmdBulletPhysics.ts#L245-L283) passes the new follow-bone target to its kinematic `MotionState` via [`RigidBodyBundle.setTransformMatrix()`](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/Bind/rigidBodyBundle.ts#L456-L488), rather than normally teleporting Bullet's kinematic body object from JavaScript each render frame.
- [Bullet `saveKinematicState()`](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btDiscreteDynamicsWorld.cpp) samples the kinematic body's MotionState when simulation substeps execute. At 120 FPS with a 60 Hz Bullet fixed step, zero-substep render frames are normal. Input timing/kinematic velocity may differ between these synchronization approaches.

This is **a hypothesis**, not a confirmed cause or a proven babylon-mmd advantage: the maintainer observed stable 120 Hz behavior in a babylon-mmd Playground but with a **different MMD model**.

## Expected outcome

**Switch the default Type-0/kinematic bone-following update path** in three-mmd-loader to a **MotionState-first** policy, similar to babylon-mmd: stage current bone-derived transforms in the kinematic body's MotionState and let Bullet sample/apply them on the next physics step. Do **not** call `setCenterOfMassTransform` to teleport a Type-0 body on *every rendered frame*.

Implement this as the new normal behavior for **standalone Sync, shared Sync and Worker Physics**. Keep it a **single isolated change** with an uncomplicated revert path; a comparison UI or optional runtime mode is **not** requested.

**Scope boundaries:** Existing initialization, explicit reset/seek/warmup, and intentional physics-state reconstruction may still need to update both native body and MotionState atomically. This task should only change **per-frame kinematic following**, not incorrectly convert dynamic bodies or disable required resets. PMD Type-2 dynamic-body position realignment is a **separate potential issue** and must not be silently changed here; PMX Type-2's existing special handling must remain intact.

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Update the Type-0 follow-bone path in `src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts`: both ordinary and PMX deferred kinematic inputs should write the current bone target to `btMotionState`, without `btRigidBody.setCenterOfMassTransform()` during routine per-frame following. Preserve the model's existing bone offsets, coordinate conversions and PMX pre/post-physics layers.
- [ ] Keep **initial creation and deliberate reset/rebuild** coherent: native body transform, MotionState, interpolation state/velocity, caches and any required activation remain synchronized so there is no stale initial/teleport pose on the next Bullet step. Explain and test exceptions to the per-frame MotionState-only rule.
- [ ] Validate compatibility with the new default **Bullet-backed Ammo WASM** introduced by PR #87, including the actual `btDefaultMotionState` binding and how Bullet's kinematic state is consumed. Avoid assumptions from babylon-mmd's separate memory/binding implementation.
- [ ] Add automated tests with a **moving Type-0 kinematic anchor linked to a dynamic body/joint**, using real Bullet on PMD and PMX. Check at least **60, 120 and 144 FPS** (including zero-substep frames and nonuniform deltas): proper MotionState staging, actual native body/velocity update on completed Bullet steps, constraint participation, finite states, elapsed-time integrity and no unintended per-render body teleport. Check that zero-step frames do *not* spuriously advance physics or lose the latest required kinematic target.
- [ ] Cover **standalone Sync, shared Sync and Worker** paths (both buffer transports where supported), reset/warmup/loop, PMX deferred inputs, Worker fallback, and existing Type-1/Type-2 behavior; adapt existing tests that previously asserted direct kinematic COM mutation. Avoid turning a valid zero-step frame into a forced physical step.
- [ ] Preserve current Bullet version and WASM backend, `unitStep=1/60`, `maxStepNum=10`, STOP_ERP, frame-offset policy, damping, gravity, collision masks, springs, bone/post-physics projection and default rendering behavior. Do **not** bundle another physics experiment or auto-clamp suspicious motion.
- [ ] Run relevant typecheck, unit/real-Bullet integration, browser tests, build/Examples build, and local built-site smoke tests; document the evidence and remaining uncertainty. Automated success **does not prove** the intermittent violent instability is fixed.
- [ ] Explain the new default behavior and simple revert approach in source/comments or a short validation document. **No maintainer visual approval is required before merge.**

### Required post-merge verification

- **PENDING until performed:** Inspect the latest attempt of merge-triggered GitHub Pages deployment. Confirm published SHA and successful publication of the new runtime/Examples; note retries/transient 503 failures accurately.
- **PENDING until performed:** Perform a basic real-browser smoke check of the newly published PMD, Gene Light PMX and Worker Physics Examples as applicable, checking backend initialization, animations, and finite controlled physics motion. Record URLs, browser and evidence. This post-merge check is **not a pre-merge blocker**.
- **Optional maintainer-led visual evaluation (not a merge blocker):** **After the new behavior is switched on**, the maintainer will inspect actual-model motion and long-running 60/120 Hz stability. Leave the visual/stability outcome **PENDING / unverified** until they report it. Do not claim the severe oscillation is solved in advance.

## Context

- Current [Type-0 and deferred sync](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts#L1148-L1177), [`_setTransformFromBone()` / reset](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/MMDPhysics.ts#L1129-L1138), [Worker input application](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/animation/PhysicsWorkerRuntime.ts#L49-L95), and [existing Ammo interface](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/ammo.ts).
- Babylon reference: [`MmdBulletPhysicsModel.syncBodies()`](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/mmdBulletPhysics.ts#L245-L283), [`RigidBodyBundle.setTransformMatrix()`](https://github.com/noname0310/babylon-mmd/blob/main/src/Runtime/Optimized/Physics/Bind/rigidBodyBundle.ts#L456-L488).
- Bullet reference: [`btDiscreteDynamicsWorld::saveKinematicState()`](https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/master/src/BulletDynamics/Dynamics/btDiscreteDynamicsWorld.cpp#L249-L267).
- This tests the effect of **how kinematic input is submitted to Bullet**, rather than changing the displayed bone's MotionState/interpolated transform output, the Bullet engine version, or Type-2 dynamics.
